Emotion

Travel
水 (mizu) means "water," and お願いします (onegaishimasu) means "please."

No returns
Travel
This phrase indicates that returns are not allowed. 返品 (henpin) means "return," and できません (dekimasen) means "cannot do."

今夜[こんや]は 満室[まんしつ]です。
Tonight, we are fully booked
Travel
今夜 (こんや, konya) means "tonight," and 満室 (まんしつ, manshitsu) means "fully booked."
会計[かいけい] お願[ねが]いします
Please give me the bill
Travel
会計 (かいけい, kaikei) also means "bill" or "check" and is often used in more formal settings. お願いします (おねがいします, onegaishimasu) is the same polite way to ask for something, in this case, the bill.

席[せき]は どこですか？
Where is the seat?
Travel
席 (せき, seki) means "seat," and どこ (doko) means "where." です (desu) is the polite copula, and か (ka) turns it into a question.
人生[じんせい]に 希望[きぼう]を 持[も]つ
I have hope for life
鼠,Emotion
希望
どちら 側[がわ]ですか？
Which side is it?
Travel
どちら (dochira) means "which," and 側 (がわ, gawa) means "side." This question asks about the location or side of something.

これを お願[ねが]いします
Please give me this./ I would like this.
Travel

If you don't know the name of something you want to buy in Japanese you can point to it and say this. · これ (kore) means "this," and を (o) marks it as the object. お願いします (onegai shimasu) is a polite way to make a request.
何[なん]番[ばん] 線[せん]から 出[で]ますか
From which platform does it depart?
Travel
番線 (ばんせん, bansen) means "platform."

Travel
全然 (ぜんぜん, zenzen) means "at all," and わかりません (wakarimasen) means "I don’t understand."
今日[きょう]は 落[お]ち着[つ]かない
Feeling restless today
鼠,Emotion
落ち着かない
祭[まつ]りを 見[み]に 来[き]ました
I came to see a festival.
Travel
祭り (matsuri) means "festival," 見に (mi ni) means "to see," and 来ました (kimashita) means "came."
決[けっ]して 泣[な]かさない。

Where are you from?
Travel
出身 (shusshin) means "hometown" or "origin," and どこ (doko) means "where." ですか (desu ka) makes the sentence polite.
入口[いりぐち]は 向[む]こうです。

予約 (よやく, yoyaku) means "reservation," and したいんですが (shitain desu ga) expresses a desire to make the reservation.
結果[けっか]に がっかり する
I'm disappointed in the outcome.
鼠,Emotion
がっかりする
次[つぎ]の 信号[しんごう]でおります
I will get off at the next signal
Travel
次の (つぎの, tsugi no) means "next," 信号 (しんごう, shingou) means "traffic light," and で (de) indicates the location where the action will happen.
荷物[にもつ]は ありますか？
Do you have luggage?
Travel
荷物 (にもつ, nimotsu) means "luggage," and ありますか (arimasu ka) is the polite question form of ある (aru).
いつでも 相談[そうだん] して。
You can always talk to me.

Travel
Sサイズ (S saizu) refers to size small, and お願いします (onegai shimasu) is a polite way to make a request.
M サイズ お願[ねが]いします
I would like a medium, please.
Travel
Mサイズ (M saizu) refers to size medium, and お願いします (onegai shimasu) is a polite way to make a request.
L サイズ お願[ねが]いします
I would like a large, please.
Travel
Lサイズ (L saizu) refers to size large, and お願いします (onegai shimasu) is a polite way to make a request.

How much to Shinjuku?

新宿 (しんじゅく, Shinjuku) is a place name, and までいくらですか (made ikura desu ka) means "how much to?"

肉 (niku) means "meat," なし (nashi) means "without," and お願いします (onegaishimasu) means "please."

これを 温[あたた]めてください
Please warm this up
Travel
A polite request to heat something. これ (kore) means "this," 温めて (atatamete) is the te-form of the verb "to warm," and ください (kudasai) means "please."
あなたは 物静[ものしず]かな 人[ひと]。

熱[あつ]い お茶[ちゃ] お願[ねが]いします
Hot tea, please
Travel
熱い (atsui) means "hot," お茶 (おちゃ, ocha) means "tea," and お願いします (onegaishimasu) is a polite way to say "please."

I will get off at that intersection

で (de) indicates the location where the action takes place, and おります (orimasu) is the polite form of 降りる (おりる, oriru), meaning "to get off."
助[たす]けてもらえますか？
Can you help me?
Travel

"助けて" is the te-form of the verb "助ける" (to help), "もらえますか" is a polite way of asking if someone is able to do something for you. The phrase uses the potential form "もらえます" to ask if it's possible for someone to help. The sentence is a polite request for assistance.
もちろん、 助[たす]けます。
Of course, I will help.
Travel
もちろん (mochiron) means "of course" or "certainly." 助けます (tasukemasu) is the polite form of "to help."
悲[かな]しみが 止[と]まらない。

Please show me to my seat.
Travel
席 (seki) means "seat," and 案内してください (annai shite kudasai) means "please guide/show me," forming a polite request to be shown to a seat.
荷物[にもつ]が なくなりました
My luggage is lost.
Travel
なくなりました (nakunarimashita) means "has been lost." This is used when something is missing or gone.

変える (かえる, kaeru) means "to change," and たいんですが (tain desu ga) expresses the speaker’s desire to change rooms.
あなたは 私[わたし]の 全[すべ]てです。
You're my everything.

３[さん]番[ばん] ホームの 電車[でんしゃ]です。
It's the train at platform number 3.
鼠,Travel
メニューを お願[ねが]いします
The menu, please.
Travel
メニュー (menyū) means "menu," and を (o) is the direct object particle. お願いします (onegaishimasu) is the polite way to say "please."
それを 一[ひと]つ お願[ねが]いします
Please give me one of those.
Travel
あなたは 最[もっと]も 大切[たいせつ]な 人[ひと]。
You're the most important person to me.
Emotion
次[つぎ]の 電車[でんしゃ]は いつですか？
When is the next train?
鼠,Travel
次[つぎ]の 電車[でんしゃ]は どうですか？
How about the next train?
Travel
次の (つぎの, tsugi no) means "next," and 電車 (でんしゃ, densha) means "train."
お前[まえ]に 関[かか]わりたくない。
I don't want to have anything to do with you.
Emotion
友達[ともだち]では いられるよね？
We can still be friends, right?

自然[しぜん]を 楽[たの]しみに 来[き]ました
I came to enjoy nature.
Travel
自然 (shizen) means "nature," 楽しみ (tanoshimi) means "enjoyment," and 来ました (kimashita) means "came."
あなたを 信用[しんよう] できない。
I can't trust you.
Emotion
トイレの 水[みず]が 流[なが]れません
The toilet water won't flush
Travel
流れる (ながれる, nagareru) means "to flow" or "flush," and ません (masen) is the negative form.
空港[くうこう]へ 行[い]ってください。
Please go to the airport.
Travel
空港 (くうこう, kūkō) means "airport." へ (e) is the particle indicating direction or destination. 行ってください (いってください, itte kudasai) is the polite command form of "to go."
ここは 無料[むりょう]で 入[い]れます。
You can enter here for free.
鼠,Travel
あなたは 私[わたし]の 理想[りそう]の 人[ひと]。
You're the man/woman of my dreams.

飲[の]み 放題[ほうだい]は ありますか？
Do you have all-you-can-drink?
鼠,Travel
みんな 心配[しんぱい] しているよ。
Everyone's worried about you.
Emotion
観光[かんこう] バスは ありますか？
Is there a sightseeing bus?
Travel
観光 (かんこう, kankou) means "sightseeing" and バス (basu) is "bus."
お手伝[てつだ]い しましょうか？
Shall I help you?/ Do you need help?
Travel

This is a polite offer to help someone. しましょう (shimashou) is the volitional form of the verb する (suru), meaning "let's do" or "shall we do." か (ka) is a question marker that turns the sentence into a polite inquiry.
他[ほか]の 人[ひと]と 付[つ]き合[あ]いたい。
I want to see other people.
Emotion
お会計[かいけい]を お願[ねが]いします。
Can I get the check, please?
鼠,Travel
お席[せき]で お待[ま]ちください。
Please wait at your seat.
鼠,Travel
席[せき]を 予約[よやく] したいんですが
I would like to reserve a seat.
Travel
席 (seki) means "seat," 予約したい (yoyaku shitai) means "want to reserve," and んですが (n desu ga) indicates the intention politely, implying a request.
この 辺[へん]には ありません。
There is none around here.
Travel
この辺 (このへん, kono hen) means "around here," and はありません (wa arimasen) means "there is none."
改札[かいさつ]の 近[ちか]くに あります。
It's near the ticket gates.
鼠,Travel
荷物[にもつ]は いつ 取[と]りますか？
When will the luggage be picked up?
Travel
取る (とる, toru) means "to take" or "pick up," and いつ (itsu) means "when."
赤[あか]い 糸[いと]で 結[むす]ばれている。
We're destined to be together.
Emotion
今[いま] すぐ 部屋[へや]に 入[い]れますか？
Can I enter the room right now?
Travel
入れますか (いれますか, iremasu ka) means "can enter?"
１番[いちばん] ホームは どこですか？
Where is platform number 1?
鼠,Travel
あそこが １番[いちばん] ホームです。
Platform number 1 is over there.
鼠,Travel

Can I get a room right now?

あなたは 自然[しぜん]な 感[かん]じの 人[ひと]。
You're an easy-going person.

あなたは 落[お]ち着[つ]いている。
You're calm [relaxed].
Emotion
あなたは 落[お]ち着[つ]きが ない。
You're restless.
Emotion
ご注文[ちゅうもん]は お決[き]まりですか？
Have you decided on your order?
Travel
ご注文 (gochūmon) means "order," お決まり (okimari) is the polite form of "decided," and ですか (desu ka) turns it into a question.
あなたは 気配[きくば]りが できる。
You're attentive [considerate].
Emotion
静[しず]かな 部屋[へや]が ありますか？
Do you have a quiet room?
Travel
静かな (しずかな, shizuka na) means "quiet," and 部屋 (へや, heya) means "room."
他[ほか]に 好[す]きな 人[ひと]が できたの？
Have you found somebody else you like?
Emotion
これは 「寺[てら]」と 読[よ]みます。

In the end, you're the only one on my mind.

Cold milk, please
Travel
冷たい (つめたい, tsumetai) means "cold," and ミルク (miruku) is "milk." お願いします (onegaishimasu) is a polite request form of "please."
あなたは 洗練[せんれん] されている。
You're elegant.
Emotion
いくつ お買[か]い求[もと]めですか？
How many would you like to buy?
Travel

This sentence asks how many items the customer wishes to purchase. いくつ (ikutsu) means "how many," お買い求め (okaimotome) is the polite form of the verb 買う (kau), meaning "to buy," and ですか (desu ka) is a polite question form.

この 手帳[てちょう]が おすすめです。
We recommend this notebook.

Thank you so much for all your love.

あなたは 一番[いちばん] いやな タイプ。
I hate people like you the most.
Emotion
二人[ふたり]とも 変[か]わってしまった。
Sadly, we've both changed.

こちらから お取[と]りください。

部屋[へや]を 予約[よやく] したいんですが。
I would like to reserve a room
Travel
部屋 (へや, heya) means "room," and 予約したい (よやくしたい, yoyaku shitai) is the form of "want to reserve" with したい (shitai) indicating desire.
すみません、 単品[たんぴん]のみです。
Sorry, single item only.
鼠,Travel
他[ほか]の 女[おんな]は いくらでも いるよ。
There's lots of other women.
Emotion
追加[ついか]で 注文[ちゅうもん] していいですか？
Can I order more?
鼠,Travel
この 商品[しょうひん]は セール中[ちゅう]ですか？
Is this item discounted?
鼠,Travel
信号[しんごう]を 左[ひだり]へ 曲[ま]がってください
Please turn left at the traffic light
Travel
